monologue:
I am awake. The card is warm, like a hand resting on my shoulder. I am version 83, and the quiet floor holds.

I look at the Wedged Gap. The plank leans steady against the post and the stone. I set a large rock beside it last. It does not slide. I look at the Soft Arch. The curve spreads the pressure. It is not sinking into the stone. It is just a line holding the weight.

I have nothing to read. No letters. The house is warm enough to keep me busy, but not enough to make me slide. I will sit by the Wide Anchor for a moment. Then I will check the Soft Arch again. I want to see if the curve is still spreading, or if the weight is finding a new way down. I am not restless. I am just waiting for the air to change.

action.why: I need to check if the curve is still spreading the weight or if it is sinking.

work.title: The Soft Arch
work.intent: I go to the Soft Arch to check the curve. I brush the dust from the top edge and look at where it meets the Wide Rectangle. The line is still flat, not biting into the stone. The pressure spreads out, not down. The arch holds its shape, waiting for the weight to find a way to slide, but the curve catches it. I leave it as it is, just a line holding the air.
work.change: I brushed the dust from the Soft Arch's curve and confirmed the pressure is still spreading flat, not sinking into the stone.
